@Zentrik:
Per the bot (which I have reviewed and seems at least mostly correct, but I don't understand this cancellation logic well enough to know if the proposed patch is what we want):

Three separate causes.

Timings are min-of-mins over 3–5 interleaved runs on an idle machine. Cross-commit rows use prebuilt per-commit binaries; unpatched/patched rows are one master build with the change toggled, so the two kinds of row are not comparable to each other. Source links pin to [`08eef75`](https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/commit/08eef7536a689b78115ac218645f66b6d0e3305a).

## `array.index` on `ReinterpretArray` **and** `string.repeat` — both #62604

`CancellationLowering`'s unsafe-point walk classifies LLVM intrinsics against a [fixed eight-entry allowlist](https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/blob/08eef7536a689b78115ac218645f66b6d0e3305a/src/llvm-cancellation-lowering.cpp#L552-L566). In a function that may be inside an open region, anything outside that list gets a volatile store to `task->reset_ctx` plus a signal fence in front of it. Three classes are caught that cannot tear a region:

- pure computation, e.g. `llvm.smax` (the one I observed), and by the same path `llvm.abs`, `llvm.ctlz`, `llvm.fmuladd`, the overflow-checked arithmetic
- the `GC.@preserve` markers, which carry the `llvm.` prefix and so arrive as intrinsics with no recognised ID, even though `LateLowerGCFrame` deletes them outright
- `llvm.memcpy`/`memmove`/`memset`, treated as calls rather than as the bulk stores they are, which is inconsistent with the [store rule](https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/blob/08eef7536a689b78115ac218645f66b6d0e3305a/src/llvm-cancellation-lowering.cpp#L505-L520) a few lines above

This lands on any function inference proves effect-free *and* reset-safe, since those get [`julia.ipo_reset_safe`](https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/blob/08eef7536a689b78115ac218645f66b6d0e3305a/src/codegen.cpp#L9238-L9245) and the walk then [treats every block as possibly inside a caller's open region](https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/blob/08eef7536a689b78115ac218645f66b6d0e3305a/src/llvm-cancellation-lowering.cpp#L449).

[`perf_sumelt`](https://github.com/JuliaCI/BaseBenchmarks.jl/blob/master/src/array/sumindex.jl#L5-L11) over a `ReinterpretArray` picks up two clears for the [`GC.@preserve`](https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/blob/08eef7536a689b78115ac218645f66b6d0e3305a/base/reinterpretarray.jl#L482-L506) markers and one for the `llvm.smax.i64` in its trip count. With those clears in the loop body, the invariant `A.parent` and size loads and the trip-count computation are no longer hoisted out of the loop, and the inner loop goes from 4 to 15 instructions. `perf_sumelt(::Array)` has no intrinsic in its loop, which is why plain arrays were unaffected.

`string.repeat` is the same bug, and it lands on #62604 rather than #62557. The sysimage's `julia_repeat_0`/`julia_repeat_1` are byte-identical across the window and carry zero clears — but BaseBenchmarks calls [`repeat` with a literal](https://github.com/JuliaCI/BaseBenchmarks.jl/blob/master/src/string/StringBenchmarks.jl#L54-L58), so const-prop yields a specialization inferring total effects (including `+re`), which BenchmarkTools compiles into a [`@noinline` core function](https://github.com/JuliaCI/BenchmarkTools.jl/blob/master/src/execution.jl#L682-L700). That JIT-compiled function goes from 0 to 22 clears — one per 16-byte copy of the unrolled [`unsafe_copyto!` loop](https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/blob/08eef7536a689b78115ac218645f66b6d0e3305a/base/strings/substring.jl#L302-L306):

```asm
L144:
  mov     qword ptr [r13 + 72], 0          ; reset_ctx = NULL
  vmovups xmm0, xmmword ptr [rcx]
  vmovups xmmword ptr [rax + rdx - 144], xmm0
  mov     qword ptr [r13 + 72], 0
  ...                                       (x10, unrolled)
```

Across the offending commit (BaseBenchmarks for the `repeat` rows, an equivalent probe for `sumelt`):

| | [pre-#62604](https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/commit/c4dc4e24b091c934451f3a7c5dc1c1609c13cf75) | [post-#62604](https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/commit/5566b23a420abd92c4d33aa57ae6e577860fd65e) | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sumelt reinterpret(Int32, ::Array{Float64,3})` | 1126 ns | 2364 ns | +110% |
| `repeat str len 16` | 390 ns | 735 ns | +89% |
| `repeat str len 1` | 29.6 ns | 36.7 ns | +24% |
| `repeat char 1` | 37.6 ns | 42.0 ns | +12% |
| `repeat char 2` | 73.0 ns | 76.1 ns | +4% |

`repeat char 2` is a useful control: it takes the `n == 2` branch, a plain `unsafe_store!` loop with no memory intrinsic in it, and it barely moves. The three that do regress all reach a `memset` or `memcpy`.

Classifying intrinsics by their own effects instead of by name fixes these: [`claude/julia-62856-diagnosis-pd6ew5`](https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/compare/master...claude/julia-62856-diagnosis-pd6ew5). Toggled on one master build:

| | unpatched | patched | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sumelt reinterpret(Int32, ::Array{Float64,3})` | 2366 ns | 1129 ns | −52% |
| `repeat str len 16` | 1113 ns | 735 ns | −34% |
| `repeat str len 1` | 40.4 ns | 31.1 ns | −23% |
| `repeat char 1` | 39.6 ns | 30.4 ns | −23% |
| `read(exhausted IOBuffer, String)` | 35.5 ns | 35.5 ns | — |

It does not cover the whole `array`/`find` picture: `simd.*` and `tuple.index.(sumelt, NTuple, 30, Float64)` are unchanged by it, and a `findprev` over a `Vector{Bool}` recovers only part of its loss. Those look like something else.

## IO — #62557

| | [311f373e](https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/commit/311f373e01209f59235de7fc32802eb72c64b9b8) | [35b7e121](https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/commit/35b7e12113efec385c19f38b2f9623fc8f2649fd) |
|---|---|---|
| `read(exhausted IOBuffer, String)` | 10.0 ns | 39.7 ns |
| `readuntil(buf, "AA")` | 41.6 ns | 55.4 ns |

[`io.read.readstring`](https://github.com/JuliaCI/BaseBenchmarks.jl/blob/master/src/io/IOBenchmarks.jl#L30) reads the buffer dry on its first eval and measures an exhausted buffer thereafter — about 10 ns of pure call overhead — which now pays a full compiled cancellation point at the [`readbytes!` entry gate](https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/blob/08eef7536a689b78115ac218645f66b6d0e3305a/base/io.jl#L1298-L1305). The same applies to `readuntil` at target lengths 1 and 2; longer targets amortise it away. `io.read.read` is flat, because only the generic `IO` fallbacks were instrumented, not the `GenericIOBuffer` specialisations.

## BigInt — #62629

| | [pre](https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/commit/c6cd168cb957c755c0e8b8d86d4847b1823bb32a) | [+#62629](https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/commit/da7776ad8f5e75e3cbddcb778a6bd16045155a2f) | master |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MPZ.add!` (no allocation) | 7.95 ns | 19.42 ns | 17.07 ns |
| `BigInt(nbits=256)` | 32.14 ns | 33.66 ns | 34.42 ns |
| `A + B` | 39.56 ns | 57.82 ns | 58.25 ns |
| `A + UInt64(3)` | 59.00 ns | 87.52 ns | 88.02 ns |

Of the ~18 ns on `A + B`, about 11.5 ns is the [`@cancel_check` now in front of every MPZ op](https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/blob/08eef7536a689b78115ac218645f66b6d0e3305a/base/gmp.jl#L167-L179) and about 1.5 ns is the [GMP allocation hooks](https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/blob/08eef7536a689b78115ac218645f66b6d0e3305a/src/gc-common.c#L659-L672) doing a task lookup and unpublish/republish per malloc; I have not accounted for the remaining ~5 ns.

Breaking the check down on the `MPZ.add!` shape, within one build. The "no check" row reproduces the pre-#62629 sysimage figure exactly, which is a useful cross-check:

| | time | vs no check | instructions |
|---|---|---|---|
| no check | 7.95 ns | — | 22 |
| `GC.safepoint()` alone | 8.54 ns | +0.6 | |
| level-triggered [`checkcancel`](https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/blob/08eef7536a689b78115ac218645f66b6d0e3305a/base/cancellation.jl#L982-L989) | 10.60 ns | +2.6 | |
| full [`@cancel_check`](https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/blob/08eef7536a689b78115ac218645f66b6d0e3305a/base/cancellation.jl#L946-L962) | 16.67 ns | +8.7 | 328 |
| full check, pass forced into [`no_publish`](https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/blob/08eef7536a689b78115ac218645f66b6d0e3305a/src/llvm-cancellation-lowering.cpp#L229-L237) | 12.43 ns | +4.8 | 192 |

So of the +8.7: about 2.6 ns is the token lookup and status check, about 3.9 ns is the reset-region publication (the `setjmp`, its volatile publish/unpublish stores, and the 136 instructions that go with them), and the remaining ~2.2 ns is the binding bookkeeping and the preempt read.

The check also turns a 22-instruction leaf into one carrying a GC frame and three extra callee-saved pushes. That is *not* the `setjmp` — the frame and the pushes are still there under `no_publish`, so they come from the slow-path call edges (`_default_cancel_token_slow`, `handle_cancellation!`) needing their results rooted.

Two changes that do **not** help, so nobody need repeat them:

- skipping region establishment when no token is bound: −0.07 ns. The source arm still contains a `setjmp`, so nothing about the function's shape changes.
- removing the `while true` retry loop from the macro: 328 → 191 instructions, 4 → 2 setjmps, for −0.65 ns. It is not code size.

A `setjmp` cannot be outlined, since the buffer has to live in the frame you land in. `Base.checkcancel` is the level-triggered form and costs +2.6 ns against the +8.7 of an establishing point.

## `alloc.structs` +8.7%

A separate arm of #62604, not covered by the patch above. In a `+re` function `julia.gc_alloc_obj` is annotated `julia.reset_region` and [rerouted](https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/blob/08eef7536a689b78115ac218645f66b6d0e3305a/src/llvm-final-gc-lowering-stock.cpp#L16-L46) to [`jl_gc_small_alloc_reset_safe`](https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/blob/08eef7536a689b78115ac218645f66b6d0e3305a/src/gc-common.c#L607-L616), which adds a task load and an unpublish/republish and [loses the narrowed memory attribute](https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/blob/08eef7536a689b78115ac218645f66b6d0e3305a/src/llvm-pass-helpers.cpp#L340-L355) the normal allocator carries. The sysimage goes from 0 to 6086 call sites of that entry point at #62604, and a loop allocating a small mutable struct regresses 32% across it.

I could not reproduce the same for `alloc.strings` — a loop allocating via `_string_n` is flat across #62604, and `_string_n` is a `jl_`-prefixed `ccall` rather than a `julia.gc_alloc_obj`, so it is not rerouted. That +8.1% is probably something else.

## On #62673

Those numbers predate it, but nanosoldier has since measured [`216c604f`](https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/commit/216c604f36413c4452f5424bcd86f358469c9ee7). It helps the two token-lookup-heavy cases and nothing else:

| | pre | peak | with #62673 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `io.read.readstring` | 12.35 | 56.97 | 45.94 |
| `scalar.arithmetic.(add, BigInt, UInt64)` | 71.71 | 109.37 | 100.86 |
| `string.repeat.repeat str len 16` | 792.9 | 1216.5 | 1218.5 |
| `array.index.(sumelt, RA{Int32,3,Float64,…})` | 916.0 | 2787.1 | 2786.1 |

## Cancellation points

# The slow path of `@cancel_check`: `st` is the (non-zero) status byte
# reported by the cancellation point.
@noinline function handle_cancellation!(src::Union{Nothing, CancellationTokenSource}, st::UInt8)
    ct = current_task()
    if st & STATUS_PREEMPT_BIT != 0x00
        # consume the cooperative-yield request
        @atomic :monotonic ct.preempt_request = 0x00
    end
    if st & SEVERITY_MASK == 0x00
        # preempt-only (a pending yield request, or a preempt shootdown that
        # reset this point): let another task run, then resume
        yield()
        return nothing
    end
    src = src::CancellationTokenSource
    # re-read: deliver the severity current at throw time, not the one the
    # fast path happened to observe
    st = @atomic :acquire src.state
    throw(CancellationRequest(st))
end

"""
    Core.cancellation_point!(src::Union{Nothing, Core.CancellationTokenSource})::UInt8

Check the cancellation state of `src` (see [`@cancel_check`](@ref)),
additionally giving the optimizer license to establish this point as a
cancellation reset point: when compiled, the source is published as the token
binding governing the current computation, and the runtime may asynchronously
unwind execution to the nearest preceding cancellation point when the source
is cancelled. Returns a status byte: `0x00` if nothing is pending, the
(nonzero) severity if `src` is cancelled, with the `0x40` bit set if a
cooperative yield (preemption) was requested.

!!! warning
    `src` must remain otherwise reachable (e.g. through the scope binding
    that supplied it, as [`@cancel_check`](@ref) guarantees) for the dynamic
    extent of the region this point establishes: copies of the binding saved
    by exception handlers are not GC-scanned.
"""
Core.cancellation_point!

"""
    @cancel_check
    @cancel_check token

Explicit cancellation point: checks whether the cancellation token governing
the current computation has been cancelled and, if so, throws the
corresponding [`CancellationRequest`](@ref). Long-running computational code
should place these in its hot loops so that it can be cancelled.

The one-argument form checks an explicitly provided
`Union{Nothing, CancellationToken}` instead of resolving the scoped default
token; use it to hoist the token lookup out of a tight loop.
"""
macro cancel_check()
    quote
        # compiled cancellation points are also GC safepoints, so that a tight
        # polling loop cannot starve a concurrent stop-the-world.
        # The loop re-executes the point whenever the slow path returns (a
        # preempt-only status yields and resumes): the slow-path call tears
        # down the point's reset region, so passing the point again is what
        # re-establishes it before the code the region is meant to cover.
        local s = default_cancel_source()
        while true
            local st = Core.cancellation_point!(s)::UInt8
            st == 0x00 && break
            handle_cancellation!(s, st)
        end
        nothing
    end
end

macro cancel_check(tok)
    quote
        local t = $(esc(tok))
        local s = t === nothing ? nothing : (t::CancellationToken).source
        while true
            local st = Core.cancellation_point!(s)::UInt8
            st == 0x00 && break
            handle_cancellation!(s, st)
        end
        nothing
    end
end

# Throw the `CancellationRequest` if `src` is cancelled (level-triggered:
# no per-task state is consulted). Unlike `@cancel_check` this is not a
# compiled cancellation point (it opens no async-interruptible region).
# This is the entry check of every blocking API taking a `cancel` keyword
# argument: it must run *before* the operation has any side effects.
@inline function checkcancel(src::CancellationTokenSource)
    st = @atomic :monotonic src.state
    st == 0x00 && return nothing
    handle_cancellation!(src, st)
    return nothing
end
checkcancel(::Nothing) = nothing
checkcancel(tok::CancellationToken) = checkcancel(tok.source)

struct CancelTokenKey <: AbstractScopedValue{Union{Nothing, CancellationToken}} end

"""
    CANCEL_TOKEN

The scoped value carrying the [`CancellationToken`](@ref) that governs the
current dynamic extent, or `nothing` if there is none. [`@cancel_check`](@ref)
checks it, and tasks spawned within a scope inherit it.

=====1040-1130
end

# The scoped-default resolution, with a per-task cache: when the task's
# `bound_cancel_default` flag is set, `bound_cancel_token` holds the source
# this lookup would resolve to under the task's current scope (or `nothing`),
# placed there by the slow path below. The flag is dropped wherever a scope
# is installed (`with` enter and its inline exit) and by cancellation points
# publishing a different source, and travels with the token through the
# exception-handler and finalizer save/restore brackets, so a set flag
# always describes the current scope (see bound_cancel_default in
# src/julia_threads.h). Reconstructing the token from the cached source is
# exact: `CancellationToken` is an immutable wrapper, so the copy is egal to
# the token in the scope.
@inline function default_cancel_token()
    ct = current_task()
    if getfield(ct, :bound_cancel_default) !== 0x00
        # the field's declared type (Union{Nothing, CancellationTokenSource})
        # narrows through the `=== nothing` check without a type-tag load
        s = @atomic :monotonic ct.bound_cancel_token
        s === nothing && return nothing
        return CancellationToken(s)
    end
    return _default_cancel_token_slow(ct)
end

@noinline function _default_cancel_token_slow(ct::Task)
    tok = nothing
    scope = Core.current_scope()::Union{Scope, Nothing}
    if scope !== nothing
        v = KeyValue.get(scope.values, CANCEL_TOKEN)
        if v !== nothing
            tok = something(v)::Union{Nothing, CancellationToken}
        end
    end
    # Cache the resolution for the current scope. The store is an untagged
    # unsafe point for CancellationLowering, so it cannot break a published
    # reset region's (region, token) coherence: any live region is torn down
    # before the store and re-established at the next cancellation point.
    @atomic :monotonic ct.bound_cancel_token = tok === nothing ? nothing : tok.source
    setfield!(ct, :bound_cancel_default, 0x01)
    return tok
end

@inline function default_cancel_source()
    tok = default_cancel_token()
    tok === nothing && return nothing
    return (tok::CancellationToken).source
end

## `cancel` keyword-argument plumbing

# The sentinel default for `cancel` keyword arguments: "use the scoped
# default token". Resolution to a concrete token happens once, at the first
# potential-block point of an operation, so fast paths never pay for the
# scope lookup. `cancel = nothing` makes a wait explicitly non-cancellable.
#
# N.B.: a resolved token (`Union{Nothing, CancellationToken}`) is passed
# through *positional* arguments internally: passing the union as a keyword
# argument builds an abstractly-typed NamedTuple whose kwcall the optimizer
# cannot devirtualize (which, among other things, breaks `juliac --trim`).
struct UseDefaultToken end
const DEFAULT_CANCEL = UseDefaultToken()
const CancelTokenArg = Union{UseDefaultToken, CancellationToken, Nothing}
const MaybeToken = Union{Nothing, CancellationToken}

@inline resolve_cancel_token(::UseDefaultToken) = default_cancel_token()
@inline resolve_cancel_token(tok::Union{CancellationToken, Nothing}) = tok

# The source of a resolved token (`nothing` stays `nothing`).
cancel_source(tok::CancellationToken) = tok.source
cancel_source(::Nothing) = nothing

# The entry check of a public API taking a `cancel` keyword argument:
# resolve the token and throw if it is already cancelled (uniformly
# level-triggered for the scoped default and explicit tokens alike).
@inline function check_cancel_arg(cancel::CancelTokenArg)
    tok = resolve_cancel_token(cancel)
    tok === nothing || checkcancel(tok.source)
    return tok
end

# The lighter entry check for APIs with a non-blocking fast path: an
# explicitly passed token is resolved and checked (throwing when already
# cancelled) right here, while the scoped-default sentinel passes through
# untouched, deferring the scope lookup - and its (level-triggered) check -
# to the operation's first potential-block point, so fast paths pay neither.
# Spelled `cancel = precheck_cancel_arg(cancel)` at the top of such APIs.
@inline precheck_cancel_arg(cancel::CancelTokenArg) =
    cancel isa UseDefaultToken ? cancel : check_cancel_arg(cancel)

"""
    readbytes!(stream::IO, b::AbstractVector{UInt8}, nb=length(b))

Read at most `nb` bytes from `stream` into `b`, returning the number of bytes read.
The size of `b` will be increased if needed (i.e. if `nb` is greater than `length(b)`
and enough bytes could be read), but it will never be decreased.
"""
function readbytes!(s::IO, b::AbstractArray{UInt8}, nb=length(b); cancel::CancelTokenArg=DEFAULT_CANCEL)
    tok = resolve_cancel_token(cancel)
    @cancel_check tok
    require_one_based_indexing(b)
    olb = lb = length(b)
    nr = 0
    while nr < nb && !eof(s)
        # token-gate between the reads (generic-IO cancel convention)
        @cancel_check tok
        a = read(s, UInt8)
        nr += 1
        if nr > lb
            lb = nr * 2
            resize!(b, lb)
        end
        b[nr] = a
    end
    if lb > olb
        resize!(b, nr) # shrink to just contain input data if was resized
    end
    return nr
end

; A function codegen marked julia.ipo_reset_safe (its own IPO effects are
; reset_safe) may be running inside a caller's reset region kept open across
; a reset_safe call, so machinery the runtime inserts implicitly - runtime
; library calls - and any call not itself tagged reset_safe eagerly drops
; the reset context. Tagged (non-implicit) calls stay spanned. Allocations
; and write barriers do not drop: sites that may execute with a region
; published are annotated with julia.reset_region instead, and FinalLowerGC
; lowers them to reset-safe runtime entry points that unpublish/republish
; the region themselves. A site on a path where the region was already
; dropped (here: after the untagged call) is not annotated. No region is
; established (no setjmp), and the region is NOT cleared at the return: it
; belongs to the caller.
define ptr @test_implicit_runtime_drop(i64 %v) "julia.ipo_reset_safe" {
entry:

; CHECK-NOT: setjmp
; CHECK: %reset_ctx_ptr = getelementptr i8, ptr %current_task

using BenchmarkTools, Random
using Base.GMP: MPZ

function perf_sumelt(A)
    s = zero(eltype(A))
    for a in A
        s += a
    end
    return s
end

mutable struct Foo
    x::Int
    y::Int
end
function perf_alloc_many_structs()
    for i in 1:100
        global b = [Foo(i, j) for j in 1:1000]
        GC.safepoint()
        Threads.atomic_fence()
    end
end
function perf_alloc_loop(n)
    local f
    for i in 1:n
        f = Foo(i, i)
    end
    return f
end

function perf_cancel_loop(n)
    s = 0
    for i in 1:n
        Base.@cancel_check
        s += i
    end
    return s
end

const A3d = rand(MersenneTwister(1), 11, 11, 11)
const RA = reinterpret(Int32, A3d)

# true if the state was raised, false if it was already at (or above) the
# severity.
# seq_cst: pairs with the (child-list publication; state read) sequence in
# `jl_new_cancel_source` - see the walk in `_cancel_walk_node!`.
function _raise_state!(src::CancellationTokenSource, sev::UInt8)
    old = @atomic :monotonic src.state
    while true
        if old >= sev
            return false
        end
        old, success = @atomicreplace :sequentially_consistent :monotonic src.state old => sev
        success && return true
    end
end

## Wait registrations (used by condition.jl and every parked wait)

# A task's registration on the things it waits for: `task` plus uniform
# {owner, next, aux} slots, one per waitable, with a waitee slot's `owner`
# holding the queue's identity (see `waitqueue`) while enqueued - the "am
# I registered, and on what" witness - and `nothing` otherwise. Field
# protection and atomicity live with the accessors ("Uniform slot access"
# below); the key liberty is that `task` and the slot owners are identity
.....
# the token in the scope.
@inline function default_cancel_token()
    ct = current_task()
    if getfield(ct, :bound_cancel_default) !== 0x00
        # the field's declared type (Union{Nothing, CancellationTokenSource})
        # narrows through the `=== nothing` check without a type-tag load
        s = @atomic :monotonic ct.bound_cancel_token
        s === nothing && return nothing
        return CancellationToken(s)

    return _default_cancel_token_slow(ct)
end

codegen: Stop CancellationLowering from taxing pure computation and allocation

The unsafe-point walk of CancellationLowering classified every LLVM
intrinsic outside a fixed eight-entry allowlist as a point that must clear
the published reset context, and so put a volatile store to
`task->reset_ctx` plus a signal fence in front of three kinds of
instruction that cannot tear a reset region: pure computation (`llvm.smax`,
`llvm.ctlz`, `llvm.fmuladd`, the overflow-checked arithmetic, ...), the
`GC.@preserve` markers (which carry the `llvm.` prefix, and which
LateLowerGCFrame deletes outright), and `llvm.memcpy`/`memmove`/`memset`,
which are the program's own stores in bulk form and belong under the store
rule the walk applies to plain stores. In a loop body the clear and its
fence also defeat LICM, so every loop-invariant computation around the
intrinsic is re-executed on each iteration.

This lands on every function inference proves effect-free and reset-safe,
since those carry `julia.ipo_reset_safe` and the walk then treats every
block as possibly running inside a caller's open region. Classify LLVM
intrinsics (and the `julia.*` address and tag computations) by their memory
effects instead of by name, exempt the preserve markers, and treat the
memory intrinsics as stores.

Separately, every allocation of such a function was routed through the
`jl_gc_*_alloc_reset_safe` entry points, whose task lookup, extra call and
unpublish/republish cost about 1.1ns per allocation - a quarter of a small
allocation - even though nearly all executions of nearly all such sites
find no region published at all. Branch on the published context at the
allocation site instead (its address is one load away), so that the plain
allocator is taken when there is none and the reset-safe entry point only
when a region is actually open; the write barrier's slow path, already
behind a branch and rare, keeps the annotation outright.

901ns, `repeat("repeatmerepeatme", 500)` from 1242ns to 817ns, and a loop
allocating a small mutable struct from 5.65ns to 4.58ns per allocation
(4.55ns without any instrumentation).

reads and writes of methods over abstract `IO`, and at the entry of the

volatile bookkeeping stores, a safepoint and the binding bookkeeping - that
